title: RAW_UNSCREENED: Embryonale Gefäßentwicklung als Zentralquelle-und-Zweigbericht
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: Aristotle's primary zoological account fixes a developmental source, two destination directions and species-dependent vessel counts; the bound f101r vessel-plus-three-paragraph layout could encode a comparative progression rather than a generic apparatus.

design.scope_description: Nur die bereits gebundene f101r-Beschreibung aus GDT812 (verschobenes unteres Gefäß, drei Absätze in zwei Textbändern, keine lokalen Labels) und die zugänglichen Aristotelian primary witnesses; kein neuer Seiten- oder Bildzugriff.
design.mechanism: A whole passage describes a developmental tree: one central origin appears first, vessels branch toward two destination systems, and the record changes branch count with the animal/developmental class.
design.unit: The three complete f101r paragraphs and the displaced lower vessel in the existing GDT812 visual/text review.
design.contrast: Vergleichender Entwicklungs-/Verzweigungsbericht versus hydraulische Apparatur- oder allgemeine Gefäßbeschreibung.
design.prediction: The embryology model predicts a single source role, an explicit two-way branch partition and a controlled 4/2/1 count contrast across organism classes; the apparatus model predicts vessel geometry, inlet/outlet or displacement relations without a species/count hierarchy.
concrete_observations: GDT812 records f101r as three paragraphs in ten lines across two visual text bands; its displaced lower vessel is real but has no local label to track.

Aristotle, History of Animals VII, records four vessels entering large animal embryos, two in smaller animals and one in very small animals such as fowl; two pass through the liver toward the great vein and two run toward the aorta.

Aristotle, Parts of Animals III, states that the heart is formed first and is the source/origin of the vessels; this supplies an ordered source-before-branches rule rather than a free vessel inventory.
linked_consequences: A developmental reading requires one source-first role and a repeated two-destination partition; the same target paragraph cannot treat every vessel as an equal peer label.

It predicts a count-changing or class-changing mark attached to the 4/2/1 cases, with a two-branch split where four vessels are described; an apparatus reading has no reason to preserve that count relation.

The displaced f101r vessel would be meaningful only if the bound paragraph order supplies a source/branch or terminal relation; absent that, it remains a layout observation and cannot support the model.
design.nearest_rival: A technical hydraulic or anatomical apparatus description in which centrality, displacement and branching are geometric positions without embryological time or organism-class comparison.
design.distinguishing_observation: Using only the existing f101r paragraph order and vessel-location record, look for a repeated source-before-branch ordering plus a non-arbitrary count/class contrast. A vessel label or displaced position alone does not distinguish the models.
assumption_costs: Aristotelian embryology is a historically relevant content analogue for this section.
The f101r three-paragraph order is meaningful rather than a layout accident.
Count/class and source/branch distinctions must be written or structurally recoverable; no absent labels may be invented.
design.strongest_likely_failure: GDT812 found no local f101r labels and the page's vessel displacement has no bound owner; the 4/2/1 source rule may therefore be impossible to observe, while GDT940 already shows that a fixed vessel-name extension lacks meaning binding.

primary_sources.locator: History of Animals VII, umbilical vessels
primary_sources.source_consequence: The source explicitly gives 4/2/1 vessel counts by animal size and a two-direction split through liver versus toward aorta.

primary_sources.locator: Parts of Animals III, heart and vessel origin
primary_sources.source_consequence: The heart is described as formed first and as the source of blood/vessels.

primary_sources.locator: De generatione animalium, Bekker Greek edition
primary_sources.source_consequence: Primary Greek witness metadata fixes the work and edition for later source checking; no target meaning is inferred.
